established.method: The fix is an ORDERING at a call site in a server-only module (app/lib/briefText.ts reads bytes.byteLength before calling the extractor, because pdfjs transfers the ArrayBuffer to its worker and detaches it). No unit test can reach it: briefText.ts imports server-only plus unpdf and mammoth, so it does not load under vitest. Redness was established empirically against the running dev server by POSTing two real PDFs to /api/briefs/extract with the size read AFTER extraction (the buggy order) and then BEFORE it (the fix).
established.evidence: Buggy order, 80,597-byte PDF stripped of all but one text line: {"text":"Background","charCount":10,"warning":null} — the scanned-PDF warning did not fire for the exact file type it exists for. After moving the read before extraction, same file: warning = 'Only 10 characters came out of a 79KB file. It is probably a scan...'. Control, healthy 924-byte PDF: charCount 299, warning null both before and after, so the fix did not just turn the warning on for everything.

attested: extractionWarning does not treat a zero byte length as a healthy empty extraction
